rows.traditional: 以 A 為母語嘅人
rows.jyutping: ji5 A wai6 mou5 jyu5 ge3 jan4
rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken construction when you want to say that someone grew up speaking A as their mother tongue.

example.english: My cousin is a native speaker of English, and she also speaks Cantonese fluently.
example.traditional: 我表姐係以英文為母語嘅人，廣東話都講得好流利。
example.jyutping: ngo5 biu2 ze1 hai6 ji5 jing1 man2 wai6 mou5 jyu5 ge3 jan4 gwong2 dung1 waa2 dou1 gong2 dak1 hou2 lau4 lei6

rows.note: Choose this concise term in education, work, or other relatively formal contexts, especially before or after a language name.

example.english: The course requires each group to include at least one English native speaker.
example.traditional: 課程要求每組至少有一位英文母語人士。
example.jyutping: fo3 cing4 jiu1 kau4 mui5 zou2 zi3 siu2 jau5 jat1 wai6 jing1 man2 mou5 jyu5 jan4 si6

rows.note: Choose this technical or written term when discussing language ability or linguistics rather than speaking casually.

example.english: For phonetic research, it is best to have a native speaker judge whether the tones sound natural.
example.traditional: 語音研究最好搵母語者判斷聲調係咪自然。
example.jyutping: jyu5 jam1 jin4 gau3 zeoi3 hou2 wan2 mou5 jyu5 ze2 pun3 dyun6 sing1 diu6 hai6 mai6 zi6 jin4
